confidence_notes: I ran five web searches: one for the RBA rate and four for Atlanta food and drink prices. Restaurant meal, coffee and beer anchors rest on Numbeo-derived figures as republished by Expatica (June 2026) and MyLifeElsewhere. Those figures were about $25 for an inexpensive meal, $105 for a three-course meal for two, $4.92 for a cappuccino and $6 for a 0.5L domestic draft. I also used Expatistan, which gave about $8 for a pub pint and about $17 for a downtown-club cocktail, and Square's bar-price guide, which gave $11-12 for an average cocktail. The beer anchor of $7 is a restaurant-serving estimate between those sources. No source gave a restaurant price for a glass of wine. The wine anchor is an inference from the Expatistan bottle price, a few individual metro-area menus ($8.50-$10.50 per glass) and a rough 1.5x ratio to beer. The cocktail anchor is about 2x beer, within the $11-$17 range found. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge, with no searches or listing checks. They are the least certain, especially the hostel figures, because Atlanta has few registered hostels, and the July 2026 window may have had World Cup-related demand spikes, which the anchors do not reflect. The FX observation came from a search result summarising the RBA exchange-rates page and RSS feed; I did not open the page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Atlanta is a large US Southeast city with mid-to-high US restaurant prices. Restaurants run about 13% above the US average per MyLifeElsewhere, and the city is cheaper than New York or Los Angeles. Accommodation is benchmarked loosely against other US Sunbelt convention and business-travel cities such as Dallas, Nashville and Charlotte.
